calls.title: MVF + GrowthBook Touch Base
calls.summary: The team agreed to conduct a limited-page trial of Growth Book to test its integration and data handling before full commitment. This initiative is driven by internal concerns about operational feasibility as emphasized by Billy Amps, who noted the necessity for practical results. The proof of concept includes a no-upfront-commitment structure, allowing the customer flexibility during the trial period with a timeline for internal readiness and legal review. The urgency is further heightened by the upcoming impression share renewal in October, creating a decision point for possibly switching platforms. The discussion highlighted the need for internal buy-in and engagement with Growth Book's engineering team, alongside the introduction of new team members to facilitate collaboration.
calls.keywords: London, GrowthBook, proof of concept, trial, integration, contract approval

calls.title: MVF & GrowthBook Trial Discussion
calls.summary:
# MVF & GrowthBook Trial Discussion
Date: 2026-09-16 | Duration: 11.529999732971191m

## Summary
The discussion evaluated a potential consulting partner that targets large clients and may support market entry rather than directly use the product. Marcel Geldner described the partner as focused on CRM implementation at customer sites, with an agency-style model distinct from existing vendors and positioned similarly to Accenture in consulting. James Shannon emphasized clarifying the business model to align expectations, resources, and collaboration workflows. The participants also addressed unexplained meeting no-shows, noting that accepted invitations were not followed by attendance or communication, which disrupted discussions and wasted team time. They agreed that unavailable participants should decline invitations proactively. James proposed monitoring no-show rates and conducting follow-ups. He tasked Marcel with investigating the partner’s role and confirming its implementation capabilities, after which the collaboration approach could be finalized. Both also agreed to reinforce meeting communication norms across teams. Sources: 04:28–06:00.

## Keywords
transcription, multilingual calls, trial feedback, proof of concept, CRM implementation, meeting attendance

## Action Items

**Marcel Geldner**
Investigate and follow up on transcription accuracy issues when switching between English and German during calls (00:16)
Conduct the introduction call with Dial at 03:00 and assess their potential role in CRM implementation partnerships or as intermediaries for entering client companies (03:24)
Follow up regarding the participant who accepted but did not join the scheduled meeting, and prepare to re-engage if they join late (05:36)

**James Shannon**
Monitor feedback from Optimizing related to the order form and their interest in a proof of concept trial (00:55)
